title: Choose the visual world for Alson Chua's portfolio
question: The roll assigned Edition of Six. Keep it, take an alternate, or re-roll.

options.label: Edition of Six
options.lineage: Fine-art print portfolios: plates pulled, signed and numbered by one hand, boxed with a colophon
options.thesis: Six works, one hand: every project signed and numbered by the person who made it.
materials: cotton rag sheet with debossed plate marks
options.viewport: A credits ledger (Idea, Design, Build, Test, Launch: A. Chua on every line) beside the current work mounted as a plate with its pencil edition line; the other five sheets stacked at the edge.
options.risk: Can turn precious or gallery-quiet if the type is timid; it must still read as someone who ships software.

raised.raise: All six works stay present at once; the chosen plate is struck forward decisively, never cross-faded.
Every work carries a catalogue number you can key directly: 1 to 6 select a plate.
Motion grows along a line: the plate mark and rules draw themselves as a print is pulled, instead of fading in.
One live registered datum: the studio clock in Malaysia (GMT+8) beside availability.
Process reads as one stage per full-width row, each with what exists after it, not five equal columns.
Labels live on the object as margin inscriptions; no floating eyebrows or section numbers.

options.label: One Line, No Transfers
options.lineage: Metro line diagrams and departure boards
options.thesis: Idea to launch on a single line with no transfers between people; six works arrived on it.
materials: single route line with station bullets
options.viewport: Huge 'One line. No transfers.' over a thick route line from Idea to Launch, with the six works listed on a departures board below.
options.risk: The most familiar of the grounded ideas: process-as-transit-map is a common metaphor and can read corporate.

options.label: Struck Cathode Gauze
options.lineage: Nixie decade counters behind anode mesh
options.thesis: Six works as unlit ghosts behind gauze, one struck forward in orange.
options.viewport: A dark plane of ghost project names with one glowing.
options.case: Fuses as a selector, but clients do not identify with lab instruments and it hides ownership.
options.risk: Moody tech costume for a developer portfolio.
options.kept: All six works present at once; the chosen one struck forward without tweening.

options.label: Teletext Service
options.thesis: The portfolio as numbered teletext pages keyed by digits.
options.viewport: P100 index with six works as numbered pages.
options.case: Clear addressing, but retro novelty undercuts the screenshots and the premium brand work.
options.risk: Reads as a gimmick to founders and brands.
options.kept: Every work holds a number you can key directly.

options.label: Secession Page
options.thesis: Ornament grows in from the margins around each work.
options.viewport: A flowering border framing the hero work.
options.case: Decorative ornament competes with the six projects' own visual worlds.
options.kept: Motion grows along a line instead of fading.

options.label: Emergency Signal
options.lineage: Broadcast colour bars and alert cards
options.thesis: The portfolio as the only broadcast left on air.
options.viewport: Colour bars with a centred alert card.
options.case: Degradation signals unreliability, the opposite of ownership.
options.kept: One live registered datum in the corner.

options.label: Power Hammer
options.lineage: Blacksmith forging under a power hammer
options.thesis: Each stage a blow that visibly lengthens the work.
options.viewport: A glowing billet with stage-by-stage measurements.
options.case: Carries process well but loses range and reads heavy-industrial for SaaS and beauty clients.
options.kept: One stage per full-width row with registered results.

options.label: Industrial Quote Grammar
options.thesis: Every zone named in straight quotes with hazard stripes.
options.viewport: Giant quoted caps naming the portfolio.
options.case: Collides with FORM / 27's fashion world and reads as a streetwear brand.
options.kept: Labels live on the object itself.

canonCard.label: The category standard
canonCard.thesis: A polished freelance developer portfolio, executed impeccably.
canonCard.viewport: Big headline, subcopy and button over a row of project thumbnails.
canonCard.risk: Indistinguishable from the competition by design.
